question.:question/problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the ellipse defined by

$$
\frac{x}{8}=\cos\theta,\quad \frac{y}{2}=\sin\theta,\quad 0\leq\theta<2\pi.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the Cartesian equation of the ellipse, we need to eliminate the parameter $\theta .$ We can do this using the Pythagorean theorem.

By squaring the $\cos\theta$ term in the $x$-equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{8} & =\cos\theta \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{(8)^{2}} & =\cos^2\theta \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{64} & =\cos^2\theta.\end{aligned}
$$

By squaring the $\sin\theta$ term in the $y$-equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{2} & =\sin\theta \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{(2)^{2}} & =\sin^2\theta \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =\sin^2\theta.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations and using $\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1,$ we get

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{64}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}=\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1.
$$

So the Cartesian equation of the ellipse is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{64}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}=1.
$$

Determine the Cartesian equation of the ellipse

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,0\le \theta <2\pi .
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the Cartesian equation of the ellipse, we need to eliminate the parameter $\theta .$ We can do this using the Pythagorean theorem.

By isolating the $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ term in the $x$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{x}{3} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{9} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

By isolating the $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ term in the $y$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ {y}^{2} & ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

 

Adding the two equations and using ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+{y}^{2} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So the Cartesian equation of the ellipse is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+{y}^{2}=1.
$$
